Nevertheless, the people soar on the wings of vain imaginings, heedless of all that causeth and bringeth about divine bounties and heavenly favors....

Today, whoever acts according to the Book of God and whose heart is purified and sanctified from doubts, hatred, enmity and all that is unworthy of man—such a one is counted among the Concourse on High. And if they attain the lofty station of martyrdom, this is the ultimate bounty for them. However, all these matters depend on the will of God, exalted be His glory. For a long time, the preservation of the servants has been revealed and recorded by the Pen of the Divine Purpose. Therefore martyrdom is rarely granted, and that only for the life of the world and the manifestation of crafts, sciences and arts. The existence of this station is like the existence of the phoenix in the regions of the world—mentioned in words but absent in deed. This servant beseeches God, exalted be His glory, to so attract all through the Kawthar of utterance that they see all else as non-existent and know it as void. A hundred thousand lives be sacrificed for His will, and a hundred thousand eternities circle round His Word....

...the friends must leave the deeds and actions of the oppressors to God and in no wise interfere. In times of hardship and tribulation they must hold fast to the cord of patience and resignation. God, exalted be His glory, Himself giveth victory and seizeth the oppressors through His all-conquering, overwhelming power. However, the friends must not be assured by any soul and must not believe every claimant to a cause, and until they find a receptive place they must not open their lips, and they must not be saddened by whatever may occur. The enkindled fire in the surroundings hath been and will be extinguished by the water of God's will, exalted be His glory. This is what the Tongue of the All-Merciful hath spoken in the Kingdom of Utterance, as a command from His presence, and He is the Almighty, the Powerful....

## BH00153: The spring of remembrance and utterance has come, yet… {.unnumbered}

### Section 1: “In the name of our Lord, the Most…” {.unnumbered}

In the name of our Lord, the Most Holy, the Most Great, the Most Exalted, the Most Glorious!

The spring of remembrance and utterance has come, yet most people do not understand. They have cast the Cause of God behind their backs, yet they perceive not. The servant laments by night and day when He sees the people behind a manifest veil. Every possessor of insight and vision is bewildered, for he observes that the people of the world attribute themselves to the Truth while remaining veiled from Him. They await the days of the Manifestation, yet are deprived of the very Manifestation Who calls out with the most exalted call. They speak of truth while clinging to creation; they speak of light while following fire. This servant knows not toward what countenance they turn, to what name they cling, what horizon they face, by what cord they move, or to what hem they hold fast.

The ocean of utterance is surging, the heaven of bounty is elevated, the Purpose is manifest—yet those souls are occupied with their own imaginings and are drowning in the seas of their vain fancies. They don turbans in the name of Truth while engaging in warfare against Him. Some turn to the synagogue while others to the mosque. If these attachments and orientations were truly for God, where are their effects? They have in truth abandoned the Synagogue of God and are occupied with the synagogues of their own souls, heedless of the circling-place of the Concourse on High, clinging to their own rejected desires. Like silkworms they have spun around themselves, yet they perceive it not. Woe unto them and away with them!

By Him Who has caused the atoms to speak His praise and glorification, if they were to reflect even less than that, they would cry out "Would that we were dust!" and exclaim "Would that we had never been born!" The smoke of heedlessness has encompassed all. At one time, the Tongue of the Lord of Names and Attributes spoke these words while revealing verses—exalted be His Word:

"O servant in attendance! Do the divines of this age imagine that in the times of the manifestation of the Daysprings of Truth, the people of the earth freely accepted the Cause of the Beloved of all creation? Do they not reflect upon the tribulations, afflictions, hardships and trials of those holy souls? Do they not ponder the blessed word ʿNo Messenger cometh unto them but they did mock at him'? What was the cause that led the Jews to rise against the Spirit (Christ) and the divines of that age to pronounce the verdict for His death? And for what reason did they rise against the Seal of the Prophets and count His companions as infidels, heedless ones and mischief-makers? Ever have the Manifestations, Daysprings and Rising-places been afflicted at the hands of enemies. Yet whatever befalls one in the path of Truth is most sweet to the soul.

"O servant in attendance! Some are observed who cling to the divine religion yet consider as false and heedless the One through Whose word the religions of the world appeared, inflicting upon Him every kind of oppression. And some believe only in what their outward senses perceive, denying all else. God curse them for their unbelief! Had they been born blind and tongueless, they would not have acknowledged the existence of anything. O servant present! The foolishness, lack of understanding and want of insight of those people has reached such a degree that one is bewildered. Say: If divine worlds were limited to this world and its manifestations, then all the Prophets, holy ones and chosen ones would have suffered loss. By Him Who caused the Tree to speak and sent down the Table! Had they known what they had done, they would have lamented in this world until they returned to their stations." End.

They do not reflect sufficiently upon this truth, that the Prophets and holy ones and chosen servants of the Almighty have, to what end, opposed themselves unto all them that dwell upon the earth. Can it be that a single soul would arise in opposition to a Cause whereto nations and governments stand arrayed in enmity, save by the command of One Who is the Mighty, the All-Powerful? This lowly servant doth beseech and implore the one true God that He may guide mankind and draw them unto the straight Path. Were they to ponder, if only for a moment, they would become enlightened; yet the smoke of heedlessness hath obscured their vision and altered the light of the heart. No person possessed of reason would abandon the eternal for that which perisheth. All bear witness to the transience of this world, yet do they cleave unto it; they observe how all return unto dust, yet remain unmindful thereof, soaring upon the wings of self and passion. Whither was I bound, and whereunto have I fallen!

My purpose is to offer reply unto that blessed epistle, and that too with brevity, lest it should prove the cause of trouble. Yet what is decreed is decreed, and the command belongeth unto God, the Sovereign of the Throne on high and of the earth beneath.

May my spirit be offered up for your steadfastness, and may my soul be a sacrifice unto your uprightness! That blessed tablet, which was inscribed upon the second day of Rabi'u'l-Avval, hath been received—praise be to God! From every word thereof was inhaled the fragrance of sincerity and love for the Beloved of all the worlds. Blessed is the leaf that is adorned with the remembrance of God, and wherein are mentioned the stations of certitude and love of the friends and loved ones for the sake of God. This servant doth not account himself worthy of mention before any of the friends, how much less in the presence of the Afnan of the Divine Lote-Tree, whom God hath related unto Himself and made them branches of His Tree. And after gaining knowledge of this matter, I purposed to attain unto the presence of the Lord of creation, and in that most sacred and exalted court was it submitted. This is what the All-Merciful hath spoken forth in the kingdom of utterance. He said, and sweeter is His word:

In the Name of the Wronged One

Praise be to God! Thou hast inhaled the fragrances of the divine days and hast turned to the Most Exalted Horizon. By the life of God! Thou art indeed under the glances of His favor—grieve not over anything. Preserve this most holy station. Hold fast unto wisdom by My command and My will. We have verily recorded thy mention in a Book which no obliteration or extinction can reach, and from which the Concourse on High shall inhale the fragrance of eternity. To this beareth witness the Mother Book. His honor Amin, that is, Abu'l-Hasan, hath arrived and repeatedly made mention of thee. He is truly adorned with love for the Afnan of the Divine Lote-Tree and expresseth great satisfaction with thee.

O Afnan! Upon thee be My glory! The whole world hath been created for the recognition of this Most Great Day, and the Ancient Beauty hath, throughout nights and days, summoned all unto the Horizon of the appearance of God, exalted be His glory. Repeatedly hath this most exalted Word been revealed from the Supreme Pen:

> "O people! Abandon wickedness and iniquity, and follow not your desires. Follow that which your Lord, the Lord of all mankind, hath revealed in His perspicuous Book."

We have forbidden all corruption, strife, contention and unseemly deeds, and have commanded that which God loveth. These matters are evident and clear to all. Nevertheless, the Name of God and His loved ones remain imprisoned in the prison of the oppressors. There hath befallen them that which hath caused the Supreme Paradise and the Most Exalted Heaven to weep. The oppression of the people hath reached such a degree as to exceed all bounds. Glory be to God! They are awakened by no event and enlightened by no punishment. A million souls in these parts have perished, yet they remain heedless. All that was revealed in the Tablet to Ra'is hath come to pass, yet they have not awakened from their slumber. The false claimant descended into hell, yet they paid no heed. The second one returned to the flames, yet they showed no remorse. And even after the seizure of the third, they may still not come to their senses. In this Revelation, God hath granted no respite—He hath seized and continueth to seize, yet none is aware.

But by God! Were it not for the decree previously ordained in the Book, He would have seized all with but a single word from Him. God hath ever desired that His creatures should exist to engage in His praise, glorification, unity and the building of His Cause, and for other purposes which none knoweth save God, the Lord of the Throne and of the dust. Some of the friends in every land were observed to be fearful. By the life of God! The world hath never had, nor hath it now, any significance. Say: Martyrdom hath a lofty station and an exalted rank. It is not vouchsafed unto everyone. It is rarer than the most precious elixir, and like unto the phoenix—its name is mentioned but its reality is hidden, nay, lost. Had they known, they would have hastened, and had they witnessed, they would have sacrificed. We have veiled this station from eyes to preserve those on earth. He guideth whom He willeth to what He desireth. There is none other God but Him, the Almighty, the Powerful. The glory shining from the heaven of My mercy be upon thee and upon My Afnan and upon those who have recognized that which God hath recognized in His exalted station.

The waves of the ocean of favor have appeared in such wise as to require no translator, interpreter or expositor. What else can this feeble servant say that would be fitting or worthy? I beseech God, exalted be His glory, to protect that noble person and to ever make him a source of service and the recipient of His favors.

All the stations of the world bow down in humility and prostration before this station. To this beareth witness every person of insight, every learned one, and every fair-minded and discerning soul.

Concerning your mention of Mulla Hasan—upon him be the glory of Baha'u'llah—and the state in which he found himself after being vouchsafed the honour of attaining unto that most august and all-protecting Tablet of the Most Holy, Divine Presence: well is it with him, and with whosoever hath discovered the fragrance of the loving-kindness of the All-Merciful in His utterance. God Himself beareth witness and is the surety thereof, that were all who dwell upon the earth to catch but the faintest breath of a single word from among the Words of God, they would, one and all, become drunken with its rapture, and would turn, illumined, unto the lights of His Countenance. Praised be God! Through the attraction of the Divine Word they have been enkindled; naught can compare with the heat of the love of God as that which is witnessed and beheld—unto this testifieth the Lord of mankind and the Possessor of the worlds of the hereafter and the herebefore.

And as to what you have written, that the revered Akhund—upon him be the glory of Baha'u'llah and His tender mercy—had, at the prompting of another, put forth those questions: in the earliest days of this Most Great Revelation, questions of every kind were presented in the Most Holy Court, and the answer to each, in full measure, was revealed and sent down according to the Will of God. But now, for some years, it hath been declared that the Supreme Pen neither inclineth to, nor occupieth itself with, the mention of answers to questions, or with matters of scholastic learning.

The Point of the Bayan—may our souls, and all besides, be a sacrifice unto Him—hath said:

> "Verily He speaketh in every matter: verily there is none other God but Me, the All-Compelling, the Self-Subsisting."

And whatsoever, in this year, hath descended from the heaven of the gracious favour of the Self-Sufficing, the Exalted, in reply to the questions of those regions, is but a token of the solicitude of God toward the steadfast in His unity and the near ones unto Him who abide in that land and its environs.

This is of the bounty of our Lord upon His branches, and upon him who hath been named by the letter Ra before Jim—upon him be the glory of Baha'u'llah, the All-Knowing, the All-Wise.

There was a time when this exalted word was revealed from the tongue of the Lord of Names:

> "O servant present in the land of Y, A and R, there are souls upon whom the eye of heaven gazeth."

This exalted word is like an ocean wherein precious pearls lie hidden. Knowledge is with God, our Lord and your Lord and the Lord of the mighty throne. Blessed is the land that hath been honored by His mention, and the cities that have attained unto His loved ones, and the light that hath derived illumination from the radiance of His chosen ones' countenance. At this point another state overtook this soul—neither having power to speak nor strength to conceal. His is the command and in His grasp is judgment. There is no God but He, the Mighty, the Powerful.

Regarding what thou didst write about the receipt document, it was sent according to the supreme instruction before, and now too it is being sent accordingly. At this moment this evanescent one was summoned to the Most Holy Court, and after attaining presence He walked for some time. After several minutes the Ancient Beauty turned His face toward the servant and said, exalted be His utterance:

> "O servant present! We have forgiven the rights of J and J and adorned them with the ornament of pardon, that they may give thanks unto God their Lord and arise to serve the Cause with wisdom and utterance."

These rights belong specifically to God, exalted be His glory.

Blessed is the soul that hath paid them and attained acceptance, and joy be to the one who, as a sign of His favor, hath been adorned with the light of forgiveness. Verily He is the One with power over whatsoever He willeth. None should hesitate in what hath been sent down from the heaven of utterance. Verily He is the Commander, the Unconstrained.

### Section 2: “After witnessing this supreme bounty, whereby the intention…” {.unnumbered}

After witnessing this supreme bounty, whereby the intention of God, exalted be His glory, was to manifest grace, this servant uttered "Thine be the praise, O Beloved of the worlds" at least a thousand times that night. It is most evident and clear that all earthly things have had and have no worth, as all have witnessed that numerous sums were repeatedly presented at the Most Holy Court but were not graced with acceptance. Yet now, in view of the gathering and the exigencies of the time, they are being accepted. In any case, the purpose was solely to manifest grace, bounty and mercy. I beseech God, exalted be His glory, to assist them to arise as befitteth the Days of God. However, according to the wisdom of His Holiness the Name of God—upon Him be all His most glorious Splendor—they have described the friends of the land of Ta, and have repeatedly expressed satisfaction, especially with some.

Yet each time they wrote that wisdom had been abandoned, and this is what is inappropriate—for they had promised this servant in various gatherings, but after attending the first gathering, it was observed that nearly fifty or sixty persons were present. I said: "Have you not heard the decree of wisdom in most divine Tablets? This decree is in effect and is recorded and written with utmost clarity." They would acknowledge this, yet on the final night the same situation was observed, and likewise in other gatherings, until finally they withdrew in seclusion. This evanescent one beseeches God, exalted be His glory, with utmost humility and supplication, that He may assist all to act according to what has been recorded in the Book by the Supreme Pen.

Every person they arrested was taken along with their writings, although divine verses should be preserved in secure and protected places. Glory be to God! What has happened? Even though this servant has mentioned this matter in numerous petitions to the friends, until now it has not been heeded. And due to the sincerity which adorns the temple of the loved ones, they accept every word and consider every claimant truthful, although in one instance this exalted Word hath shone forth from the highest horizon: "Believe not every speaker, nor trust in every newcomer." This servant hopes that henceforth they will be assisted to do what God loveth.

Concerning what you wrote about the spiritual beloved, Jinab-i-Varqa—upon him be the glory of God and His favors—God willing, they are protected and assured through God's grace, exalted be His glory. This very night, this evanescent one heard mention of them from the Most Holy Tongue. Repeatedly during the revelation of verses, favors have been shown to them. God willing, they are successful and assisted in mentioning God, serving the Cause, uniting hearts, and exalting the Word in such wise that from all their limbs, members, and veins the flame of detachment may be made manifest in the path of the Lord of creation. Glory be to God! Although no corruption appeared from them and they called heedless souls to the Dayspring of divine unity with utmost love, nevertheless the heedless divines and idle ignorant ones did what no oppressor had ever done, striving with all their might to extinguish the light of the Cause. But alas! Alas! Who can alter what God hath purposed, and who can outrun His commands? By the life of our Beloved and our Goal, they persist in their ancient error.

As to what was written concerning the Mashriqu'l-Adhkar, this matter must be kept most confidential, in such wise that none save steadfast, firm, upright, contented and well-pleasing souls may become aware of it. All these deeds are, before the Throne, contingent upon wisdom. That which opposeth it is not permissible. This is what the servant hath heard with his own ear from the tongue of God, the Self-Subsisting, the All-Compelling.

The people are weak and heedless, while grace, bounty and mercy are beyond reckoning. The Command of wisdom itself beareth witness to the loving-kindness, bounty and mercy of the Goal of all beings.

As to what thou didst write concerning the ascension of His Holiness Ismu'llah Javad, upon him be all the most glorious Glory and all the most effulgent Light, the servant testifieth that he attained unto the bounty of his Most Glorious Lord and ascended unto the Supreme Companion. The near ones perceived from him the fragrance of the mercy of our Lord and his Lord, the King of Names, and there was revealed for him from the Supreme Pen that which shall endure as long as God's most beautiful names endure. O thou beloved of my heart and Essence of God standing firm in the Cause! This is the day of death, for man attaineth unto a remembrance that hath no peer or likeness, and is adorned with a crown that shall forever shine forth, radiant and luminous throughout the world. Blessed is the soul that ascendeth through divine love; if it attaineth not martyrdom, at least it attaineth this station. Although the true friends who have quaffed from the cup of steadfastness have attained unto all good and are recorded and inscribed before God among the letters of the Book—and the letters of the Book can neither be erased nor touched by extinction—the Command is in His grasp. He doeth as He willeth and ordaineth as He pleaseth.

As to what was written about various groups being present at the funeral procession, this was presented before the Ancient Beauty, and He said:

> "They are but one people. None should attend save the people of Baha, for whom was created the Crimson Ark mentioned in the Qayyumu'l-Asma."

As to the mention made of Mirza ʿAli, upon him be the Glory of God, and what was written regarding his repeated mention of constructing monuments—this found acceptance before the Throne. Although his honor looketh unto the truth and is eager to serve, yet consideration of wisdom is necessary in all circumstances. Verily, the servant giveth him glad tidings of his remembrance in the Prison and of God's bounty, the Lord of all worlds.

As to the mention made of His Holiness Ismu'llah M.H., upon him be all the most glorious Glory, and the acquisition of land in the land of Ta [Tehran]—at present this matter is suspended in the heaven of divine Will, and after tranquility prevaileth and the kindled fire is extinguished, that which is adorned with the ornament of God's will, exalted be His glory, shall appear according to His command.

Concerning the funds of His Name 66 (Allah), JM, may all the Most Glorious Glory rest upon him, they wrote that previously this matter had issued from the Supreme Pen and was adorned with acceptance. His Name mentioned above purchased a house, and some funds remained. A portion they used to pay their debts and loans, and another portion they spent in the path of God until they arrived in the Land of Purpose. Now they and their family reside near the mansion which is outside the prison where the Throne is established, and they are engaged in pilgrimage. Praise be to God, they attained to that which they had been seeking from God, exalted be His Glory, during the nights and days. This matter of purchasing the house and giving funds was repeatedly presented at the Most Holy Court, and each time manifestations of favor towards Afnan 202 (Muhammad ʿAli), may all the Most Glorious Glory rest upon him, were evident. In truth, they are engaged in service, although outwardly some apparent causes brought them sorrow, and this is what I heard with my own ear from an informed source. However, He said:

> "God has ordained for him a station which none knoweth save God, and its effects shall appear in the world. He is, verily, the All-Knowing, the All-Wise."

This concludes the response to your first letter. Then your second letter was honored to arrive, which began with mention of the oppression that befell the innocent ones, the chosen ones, and the pillars of the earth. Has any harm come to anyone from these oppressed ones, or have they taken anyone's property, or have they uttered anything contrary to what God hath ordained? If you were to ask about this, their answer would be naught but transgression and rebellion against God, the Protector, the Self-Subsisting. Consider how this community seeks the good of government and nation during nights and days from God, exalted be His Glory. Nevertheless, there hath come upon the people of Baha from these two parties that which caused the Concourse on High to weep and lament.

One day Jesus Christ, son of Mary—may the spirit of all else be sacrificed for Him—asked the Jews, saying: "For which of my good words do you rise up to harm me?" They replied: "Not for your good words, but because you say ʿI am the Son of God."' Their condition is evident. Our shortcoming is that we say we are the people of God and are sanctified and purified from hatred, malice, corruption, conflict and contention. The flame of hatred is kindled from every direction, but the hand of power extinguisheth it with the water of will. Verily, He is powerful over all things.

Your third letter brought joy and strengthened the spirit. Praise be to God, you are adorned with the ornament of health and are engaged in serving the Cause. Regarding what you wrote about the funds for the Doctor, may the Glory of God and His favors be upon him, this matter depends on his own news. All that you have done and written regarding the house and regarding His Name Allah (Baha), may all Glory rest upon him, is correct and acceptable and is mentioned before the Throne. The servant wishes to praise God with a thousand hundred tongues and beseech from His wondrous grace your assistance, your success, and your protection. Verily our Lord, the Most Merciful, is the Powerful, the Mighty, the Unconstrained.

Glorified art Thou, O Thou through Whose manifestation the Balance hath called out and the Path been established, the mountains have passed away, and the Tongue of Utterance hath spoken in the Kingdom of Knowledge! This is the Day of Return, and the Self-Sufficing, the Most High, hath come. I beseech Thee to protect Thy Afnan from the evil of Thine enemies, to draw them nigh unto Thee, to grant them the bounty of meeting Thee, and to ordain for them the good of this world and the next through Thy generosity and grace. O my Lord! Thou seest them turning unto Thee and clinging fast unto Thee. I implore Thee, by the fragrances of Thy Revelation, to assist whosoever hath arisen to serve Thee and to aid Thy Cause. Then ordain for him that which befitteth Thy Revelation and Thy days. Verily, Thou art the Omnipotent over whatsoever Thou willest, and within Thy grasp are the reins of all who are in the heavens and on earth.

Concerning what you wrote about the beloved Varqa, upon him be the Most Glorious Beauty of God, let him be ever mindful of wisdom in all circumstances. The ignorant masses and the calumniators, especially those evil souls who remain idle and unemployed in this world, wait day and night to seize upon any pretext to inflame their base desires and passions. May God destroy them for their sins, their hypocrisy, and their unbelief. May God protect us and you from the evil of such as these. Such souls are like hot ashes that have come out of the fire—soon their heat will cool and the devastating, sterile winds will return them to nothingness. In the Tablet of Burhan, addressing the Wolf, He says:

> "Thou art like the shadow of the sun cast upon the mountains—soon it shall pass away,"

to the end of His utterance—exalted be His grandeur, sweet be His words, and great be His glory!

As for what you mentioned regarding Aqa Mas'ud and what he sent, Jinab-i-Amin, upon him be the Glory of God, forwarded his letter to the Most Holy Court where it was presented before His presence. He commanded that the honored Afnan should write him in reply and express divine favors on behalf of the Truth, that he might rejoice and be among the thankful.

Regarding what you wrote about Haji Sayyah, upon him be the Glory of God, and your expression of satisfaction with him—praise be to God that he was enabled to serve the Cause and assist the oppressed, namely those souls who themselves witness and testify that they have looked to naught but the Truth and desired naught but the reformation of the world. Blessed be he! God willing, may he ever attain this supreme bounty. The servant gives him glad tidings of his Beloved's mention of him and His favors towards him, and beseeches his Lord to assist him in all conditions. Verily, He is the Omnipotent, the Most High.

This servant's further submission is that if any of God's friends attains to service, convey my greetings to them. God willing, may the dark dust of the world of oppression not prevent them from the effulgences of the lights of justice. Every deprived and heedless one hastens toward extinction while behind him the angels of punishment cry "Hasten! Hasten!" But soon those wretched, wandering, unconscious ones shall come to their senses and cry out "Oh, woe unto us!"

May the glory shining from the heaven of our Lord's favor—your Lord and the Lord of all who are in the highest and the lowest—be upon you and upon those who love you and upon every steadfast and upright believer. Praise be to God, the Most High, the Most Great.

The servant 14th of the month of Sha'ban the Magnificent 1300

Another request: in obedience to the command, if it be possible, let the sum of fifty tumans be conveyed, in the land of Hadba, unto His Honour Ismu'llah Zaynu'l-Muqarrabin—upon him be Baha'u'llah's Most Glorious splendour. This matter is exceedingly acceptable, and is indeed most necessary, for they are in distress. ...

Another request: certain articles from the land of Kha—such as brocade, and shawls, [sugar] and the like—have been received; and Haji Mirza Abu'l-Hasan hath written, and is writing, unto Aqa ʿAzizu'llah the details thereof. The glory be upon your presence.

## BH02429: Praise be to God Who has illumined the world… {.unnumbered}

He is God, exalted be His glory, the Most Great, the Most Powerful

Praise be to God Who has illumined the world with the resplendent lamp of His Cause. And peace and blessings be upon him whose advent adorned the night journey, and upon his family and companions whom God made manifestations of His Most Splendid Name. And now, my spirit be a sacrifice for your remembrance. The servant has received your letter which spoke in remembrance of God and His chosen ones and pure ones and loved ones. I beseech Him, exalted be He, to assist your honor and our brothers there in remembrance and praise and steadfastness, the like of which has no parallel in the kingdom of creation.

As for what your honor mentioned regarding the one who was in Port Said—excellent indeed was what you did for him. Praise and thanks be to God for enabling you to assist the believers and the righteous. I convey to your service that the honored physician and the prisoner and the blessed one, upon them be the peace of God, the Mighty, the Praised—they are remembered before the Lord. Soon He will send what will gladden them.

And regarding what you mentioned about Haji Ali from K, the servant has presented what your honor wrote before the Presence. The Lord said:

> "O Muhammad-Qabli-Mustafa, upon you be My peace and My glory. We send greetings to him and to the other Ali from T whom We sent here to trade and be among those who earn. And We permitted Ali of Kashan what he desired on condition that you do not strengthen them with a third. They must engage in their work silently and quietly. They are not to speak about any matter. We beseech God to protect them and assist them in what He loves and is pleased with."

End quote. O beloved of my heart, the servant wishes to expend an island of pens and an ocean of ink in your remembrance and praise and your arising to serve the Cause, but has not found the opportunity. The matter is in the hand of God, the Lord of creation and Dawning-Place of the light of oneness.

And at the end of the letter the servant sends greetings upon his eyes and tongue and limbs and pillars and the fragrances of his heart and the radiance of his brow—Abbas and Haji Ali from T and Haji Ali from K and Mirza Husayn and Muhammad Ibrahim and the other brothers, upon them be the peace of the All-Merciful. And I beseech Him by the One through whom He illumined the world to draw them near to Him in all conditions and assist them in His remembrance and praise and in acting according to what they were commanded in His Book. And I end my words with mention of the delight of eyes, Husayn Effendi and his brothers. And peace and mercy and glory be upon your honor and upon the righteous servants of God. And praise be to God, the Lord of the worlds.

The servant 18 Sha'ban al-Mu'azzam 1300

## BH01076: Praise be to God Who hath ordained traditions… {.unnumbered}

In His Name, exalted be His station, the Grandeur and the Power!

Praise be to God Who hath ordained traditions and established laws openly, and made their source the Essence of existence and His Book sent down to him who was invested with the mantle of divine presence, through whom the mention of prophethood was sealed and there began that which draweth men nigh unto the Lord of creation. And the prayer rising from the horizon of the will of our Lord, the All-Merciful, be upon him and his family and his companions who turned toward the House and circled round it and entered through its gate. They are the emblems of victory and the standards of the Cause. Through them was the edifice of divine knowledge made firm in the contingent world and the light of the Cause shone forth amidst the concourse of religions. Blessed is he who hath heard their words and found solace in their company and clung to their hem and held fast to that which they possessed. And woe unto him who was heedless and turned away and denied.

Verily doth the servant, throughout the nights and days, beseech God to exalt His religion and manifest His proof even as He manifested it aforetime, and to honor His loved ones and chosen ones after the abasement which caused the dwellers of Paradise and the denizens of the retreats of nearness to lament. Verily He is the One with power over whatsoever He willeth. There is none other God but Him, the Single, the One, the Powerful, the All-Knowing, the All-Wise.

Thereafter, the servant attained unto your letter which began with the mention of God, our Goal and your Goal, our Object of worship and your Object of worship, and the Object of worship of all who are in the heavens and on earth. When I received it and read it and understood it, I hastened to the place of circumambulation and presented that which you had uttered by the tongue of your Lord. Then He spoke, and His sweetest utterance was:

> "O thou who art present before the Countenance! The Wronged One hath heard that which the tongue of love hath spoken in the kingdom of creation. Blessed is he who revealed it and he who read it and he who heard it and he who sent it. O Yahya! The Wronged One remembereth thee and remembereth His loved ones there who were beneath the glances of His grace. We send Our greetings from this station to them and to My loved ones and friends in the land of Sad and other regions. And We remember and send Our greetings to the people of the House, and We beseech God to draw them nigh unto Him in all conditions and to provide them with the best of beginnings and endings, and to ordain for them the Kawthar of reunion. Verily He is the One with power over whatsoever He willeth through His word ʿBe' and it is. There is none other God but Him, the Protector, the Self-Subsisting."

Praise be to God! Divine favors have been and are bestowed upon them. His grace hath encompassed them and His mercy hath preceded them. All that hath been manifested concerning them is a speaking witness and a truthful testimony. This ephemeral one offereth greetings and glorification to each one of them.

Concerning what the honored Leaf—that is, the esteemed sister, upon her be Baha'u'llah's glory—had written requesting mention of them in the Most Holy Presence: On Monday morning, the twentieth of the revered month of Sha'ban, this servant was present before Him and submitted mention of them. He expressed such loving-kindness toward them and all the household members, both female and male, that this servant is incapable of describing it. God is witness that such utterances were revealed that were they to be cast upon a mountain it would crumble from longing, were they upon the seas they would surge, and were they upon hearts they would melt. God willing, may they be joyous in all conditions and remain engaged in the remembrance of God, exalted be His glory.

And concerning their expression of regret at not receiving the missive from the household members, upon them be His most glorious splendor: their missive, at the time of departure from the first location, attained the utmost bounty. The humility of the honored sister, upon her be the glory of God and His loving-kindness, is considered as a goodly deed. One sigh in separation from God, exalted be His glory, can rend asunder a hundred thousand veils and reach the ultimate station. Blessed be the sigh and the grief that appear and manifest in His path. In any case, their deeds were presented and accepted. Happy are they, and the subsequent missive will also, God willing, attain to a glory unprecedented.

Concerning their mention of Aqa Mirza Fadlu'llah and Aqa Muhammad Hasan, upon them be the glory of God, and their degrees of longing: praise be to God, they have inhaled the fragrances of loving-kindness and attained to mention. Blessed be they both.

Concerning their mention of the esteemed aunt, upon her be the glory of God, and her purpose: it was presented and He said:

> "Our Lord! Forgive me and those who have appeared before the Countenance and her and her sister's son."

This ended. This is a great glad-tiding. God willing, may all attain the robe of forgiveness. We continually beseech this from God, exalted be His glory, and it will surely be adorned with the honor of acceptance. With the All-Bountiful, no matter or deed is difficult. All affairs are within His mighty grasp. He doeth what He willeth and ordaineth what He pleaseth, and He is the Powerful, the Mighty.

To the gentlemen who are present in that land, I convey greetings and glorification to all, and I beseech God, exalted be His glory, to gather all once again beneath the shade of the Tree. These days are the celebration of one of the Most Exalted Names—everyone's place is empty, but this servant, in lieu of congratulations, is engaged in praise and glorification in the Most Exalted Place of Security, and on behalf of those gentlemen offers congratulations and felicitations, and sometimes on their behalf, if sweets come his way, partakes of them, for He has said that our celebrations are now like the celebrations of the angels of heaven—meaning the outward means are absent as they are, but praise be to God, the true good endureth with the endurance of the Kingdom. Peace be upon you and upon God's righteous, sincere, and unified servants, and the mercy of God and His blessings.

The servant, 20th of the revered month of Sha'ban 1300

## BH01578: Praise be to the Intended One Who offered… {.unnumbered}

He is God, exalted be His glory, the Most Great, the All-Powerful

Praise be to the Intended One Who offered the living waters of knowledge to all on earth without distinction or regard for station. Among the people are those who, having turned to Him, found; who, having been commanded, took; and who drank in His Name, the Mighty, the Generous. And among them are those who turned away and denied, until they arose to extinguish the light of God, the Lord of the worlds.

May the manifest and evident prayers from the horizon of God's loving-kindness, and the radiant, brilliant peace from the direction of His mercy which preceded all things, be upon the Sovereign of the chosen ones through whom earth and heaven were illumined, and upon His family and companions who strove in God's path until His word was exalted among all beings and the necks of the servants bowed before it.

To continue: may my spirit be a sacrifice for your love—the letter of the beloved of the heart, his honor the Shaykh, upon him be 9 66 [Baha'u'llah], was noted. Praise be to God, they are adorned with the ornament of health, acceptance and love. This evanescent servant at all times and seasons beseeches and implores the True One, exalted be His glory, for the elevation of their station. After reviewing it, it was presented to the Master Who said:

> "We beseech God, the Lord of earth and heaven, to strengthen him, make him successful, and grant him the good of this world and the next. Verily He is the Master of creation, there is no God but Him, the Mighty, the Powerful. Peace be upon him and his brother and their families in Qaf. We beseech Him, exalted be He, to protect them from the darkness of smoke. Verily He is the One with power over whatsoever He willeth through His word ʿBe' and it is."

And regarding the mention they made of the honored lady, the sister of Aqa Mirza ʿIsa, it was presented and He said:

> "The True One, exalted be His glory, created all servants, both male and female, specifically for His knowledge. Blessed is the one who became aware of the cause and purpose of their creation, such that the oppression of oppressors and the opposition of unbelievers did not prevent them from the divine religion. Disbelief has encompassed the world, and the Truthful Informer has given this news. We must, in the night seasons and at dawn, at sunset and sunrise, with utmost humility and supplication beseech and implore the True One, exalted be His glory, to protect His loved ones with the hand of His providence and preserve them from the hosts of misbelief, disbelief, doubt, uncertainty, conjecture and idle fancies. Verily He has power over all things. Blessed is the leaf that heard the rustling of the Divine Lote-Tree and held fast to it, and woe to the heedless ones, both men and women."

We convey greetings to his honor ʿIsa and counsel him to that which is befitting. The first thing incumbent upon the friends of God is to purify their hearts from rancor and hatred, to sanctify and cleanse themselves from bestial qualities, and to act upon the divine ordinances with the utmost joy and fragrance. By the life of God! If they hear the call of the Wronged One, ere long the world will be seen as one homeland, tongues as one tongue, and hearts as one heart. Blessed is he who holds fast to that which benefits him and turns away from every ignorant remote one.

And regarding the mention of permission on behalf of the handmaiden of God—this matter is not permissible in these days even outwardly, as quarantine exists in the surrounding areas and means of prevention are evident. We beseech and implore the True One, exalted be His glory, to enable all His servants to attain pilgrimage or record in their book the reward of pilgrims. Verily He is the Forgiving, the Generous. There is no God but Him, the Single, the One, the Mighty, the Merciful.

Furthermore, let that beloved one act in whatever way they deem advisable. If expedient, they may send this very letter, or a copy of it, or a copy of parts of it. Verily the servant fears to contravene the wisdom he has been commanded to observe. Peace be upon you, and the mercy of God, and His blessings. The end belongs to the God-fearing, and praise be to God, the Lord of the worlds.

The servant Tuesday night, 28th of the month of Sha'ban the Great, year 1300

## BH00488: My spirit be a sacrifice for your love!… {.unnumbered}

He is God, exalted be His station, Grandeur and Power

My spirit be a sacrifice for your love! The letter from that beloved of heart and soul arrived and was presented in the Kingdom of Utterance. He said: "Praise be to God, the name of Jud, upon him be Baha, has attained divine favors. From the hand of power, wondrous signs have appeared this year—some are aware and others heedless. May the Truth make all aware, so that after becoming conscious they may testify that the people of Truth have appeared among creation for the reformation of the world and education of nations. However, no one is truly aware of this station as it is, therefore some ignorant clerics have issued decrees that have caused the dwellers of the highest Paradise and the supreme Heaven to lament and wail.

Corruption and tyranny have ever appeared from these heedless souls. Some who have drunk from the ocean of guidance are like sight for the temple of the world, while others are like smoke, becoming a veil between eyes and the witnessing of the lights of Beauty. God curse them! As you have witnessed and continue to witness what they have inflicted upon the friends of God and His chosen ones in the land of Ta. They imprisoned the Name of God without any crime or sin by the decree of those evil, heedless souls. Likewise Jinab-i-ʿAli-Qabl-i-Akbar, upon him be Baha, who ever called the ignorant people to the ocean of knowledge, and also Jinab-i-Abu'l-Fadl, upon him be Baha, and Jinab-i-Rida, upon him be the Glory of God, Master of Names. The heedless ones kindled a fire, but God extinguished it through His power and sovereignty. Thus was the matter decreed from before.

O Jud! Jinab-i-Siyyid Taqi arrived. The servant present submitted your letter, and the Wronged One, from the direction of the palace, turned toward you speaking these words: Ask of God, exalted be His glory, to cause all to attain to what He loves and is pleased with, and to draw people from the left hand of heedlessness to the right hand of awareness. Verily He has power over all things. As for your desire to attain Our presence, be patient until the Wronged One brings you other news. Convey greetings to all the friends in that land and say: By God's life, you have not been and will not be forgotten from sight. Strive that sometimes, purely for His sake and gazing toward His horizon, a deed might appear from us and you that may truly become the most exalted cause. Deeds of souls are witnesses and testifiers—they testify in the world without tongue, take without hands, and grant deliverance. We beseech God to unite us with them in spirit and fragrance, and He has power over what will be and what has been.

Praise be to God, the favor of the True Beloved is more evident than fire upon a mountain and more manifest than the shining of the sun—apparent, radiant, dawning and evident. There has not been and is not any need for the mention of this evanescent one.

In response to the request of that beloved one, and likewise in view of the days of fasting, they have returned. The cherished letter from his honor the Shaykh, upon him be the Glory of God and His favors, arrived bearing blessed tidings with joyful news—blessed be he! In his letter he mentioned the loved ones of God who had attained the bounty of imprisonment in the land of Rasht. Verily this servant gave glad tidings to all of the extinguishing of the fire. He also made mention of the five Sayyids, upon them be the Glory of God. Specifically for the loved ones of Rasht, wondrous and sublime Tablets were revealed both before and after. His honor Ismu'llah, upon him be all the most glorious Glory, had presented all their names in the Most Holy Court. And the pure and sincere deeds that were manifested by the honored Sayyids, upon them be the Glory of God—namely the giving of fifty (units of currency) to the aforementioned person, as well as another person's charitable giving according to what was written by Ismu'llah—were adorned with the ornament of acceptance. This exalted word was revealed:

> "Blessed are those souls who in these days have attained to charitable giving, and blessed is that wealth which has attained to this bounty."

Today the payment of Huququ'llah is a most momentous deed. A hundred thousand blessings upon those souls who have held fast to the Book of God and acted according to it. The mention of them, and the mention of the house wherein dwelt Ismu'llah, and those souls who were engaged in service, and those who met in love, was made in the prison in such a manner that this servant and his like are incapable and inadequate to describe it. Praise be to the Goal of all the worlds, Who enabled those cherished souls to attain that which hath no like nor equal. What more can I say? Regarding the mention of his honor ʿAndalib, upon him be the Most Glorious Glory of God—when news arrived of his imprisonment and that of the other friends, this servant clung to the hem of the robe of his Lord's mercy, the Forgiving, the Bountiful. Although God is witness and testifier that imprisonment and incarceration and the like in the path of God are more excellent than the deeds of all who are on earth, as this exalted word hath repeatedly been heard from the Kingdom of Utterance, yet due to certain considerations and the fire of love, one involuntarily seeks deliverance for the oppressed.

We beseech God to adorn all with the rewards of certitude and assurance, that they may not be fearful or disturbed by the trials of earth which in truth have no reality, though their fruits are realized and established in the realm of earthly dominion and the book of the world and the Book of the Highest Heaven. In these days He saith in certain utterances that martyrdom is like the greatest elixir and the philosopher's stone—in these days mentioned but not found—which hath not been and will not be the portion of everyone. Would that, would that this servant had been in the land of Sad and there had befallen him what befell the Essence of the Kingdom of Creation and the King of Martyrs! But the matter hath been decreed, and this ephemeral one remaineth in his regret.

Praised be God that mention of the friends at Rasht has been concluded. Multiple letters from them arrived, and what they composed in praise and tribute has wafted like fragrance in the school of divine knowledge. Repeatedly were they mentioned, but until now, due to wisdom, no response was sent. As it happened, this servant also did not submit anything, but heart and soul and vision were attentive—and God is sufficient as witness. Concerning mention of him who ascended unto God, that which draws hearts to the ocean of assurance and bestows the chalice of certitude upon souls became manifest. The appearance of every matter depends upon its appointed time. We beseech God, exalted be His glory, to grant supreme joy to all and keep them happy in the shadow of His grace. Verily our Lord, the All-Merciful, is powerful over all things and worthy to answer prayers.

O my beloved! Heedlessness has overtaken the world. It is due to the deeds of the servants that the manifest religion and the Law of the Prince of Messengers has been weakened, to such extent that the temple of the Law, established among nations upon earth—everyone snatches away one of its members, and none can prevent it, nay rather, none can even question it. A hundred thousand eyes are needed to weep for the radiant Faith. Beseech God to assist His religion. Had the people's deeds been in accordance with the glorious Law, it would certainly not have been weakened nor would it have been witnessed in such abasement. Most are heedless and veiled. Nevertheless, they have risen against those souls who spoke for God's sake, who continue to speak for God's sake, and who, for the education of the world, have borne afflictions and trials in God's path.

With utmost tyranny they have seized some, banished some, imprisoned some, and plundered and killed others—every kind of torment have they inflicted upon these holy souls. This servant beseeches God his Lord to assist His servants to act according to what is commanded in His Book, by the honor of the Prophets and Messengers. And peace be upon you and upon God's sincere servants. Praise be to God, Lord of the worlds.

Another submission: His honor the Shaykh, upon him be God's peace and favors, had written regarding Haji Ahmad and his son, upon them be the glory of God. They had previously received permission to proceed—God willing may they attain their goal. Likewise mention was made of funds; if cash arrives it would be better, as that beloved one is aware of the affairs of this land. This servant, due to wisdom, especially did not submit anything to my beloved, His honor the Shaykh—upon him be all the most glorious glory. Praise be to God, they are mentioned and are distinguished by and have attained special favors. Peace be upon him and God's mercy and blessings.

The Servant, On the night of the twelfth of the blessed month of Ramadan, year 1300. The end.

## BH06294: Your letter was received. Praise be to God, it… {.unnumbered}

He is God, exalted be His station, the Greatness and the Power

Your letter was received. Praise be to God, it indicated your health and well-being. Regarding what you wrote about traveling to Persia—you came of your own accord and now too you are free to choose. In any case there is no harm in these matters; there is freedom. However, it does not appear that Persia would be better than here. You will go and you will see. In every place one must rely on means, trusting in God. In any case, the details of your desire were presented. They said it is very good—let them come and act according to their own will. We beseech God to assist His loved ones and aid them in what He loves and is pleased with, and to make known to them what benefits them in this world and the next. Verily He is the Lord of creation and the Sovereign of Oneness. There is no God but Him, the Mighty, the Powerful. Convey this servant's greetings and praise to each of the friends. God willing, may you be joyful and adorned with the primary blessing which is health. Peace be upon you and the mercy of God and His blessings.

The servant, 11th of the blessed month of Ramadan 1300

## BH01750: Praise be to God Who, should He decree "nay… {.unnumbered}

He is God, exalted be His glory, to Whom belong greatness and power!

Praise be to God Who, should He decree "nay" for anyone, it would be sweeter than possessing the kingdom of earth and heaven, and should He decree "yea," one would choose it over the dominion of the first and the last. He is the Almighty Whom no decree of negation can frustrate and no command of affirmation can exalt. Exalted is the Lord of names and attributes, the Manifestor of clear proofs and the Revealer of verses, Who has made His Book a lamp for all creation and a guide for His servants. He is the One Who calls to goodness and commands His servants to observe it, Who has made evil manifest and forbidden people from it. Glory be unto Him! He has revealed the ordinance of religion and made His Cause manifest to those who are firm and assured, who shall fear no grief or sorrow.

May the peace that shines from the horizon of the Abode of Peace be upon the Pride of all beings and the Treasure of all existence, through whose Book the pages and tablets have been adorned, and to whose name the Prophets and Messengers have bowed down, and upon his family and companions who cast aside vain imaginings through His power and embraced certitude through His command and will.

O thou who art mentioned in the heart of this servant, O my beloved and my cherished one! This evanescent one has received your letter and presented it before His countenance, and the Beloved spoke that which I am unable to relate to you. However, when news of your arrival came like an electric current, a reply was immediately sent stating that if you desire to attain His presence, permission has been granted both before and after. This servant was assured by this reply and did not venture to send another letter. After some time, another missive arrived from that beloved one requesting a response, which caused much surprise since there had been no delay in replying and after that telegram there was nothing further requiring response. In any case, I again engaged in electrical communication and sent the final telegram.

Today, which is the thirteenth day of the blessed month of Ramadan, while I was at the farm just after arising from writing and returning to my quarters, a letter arrived from Haji Siyyid Javad, upon him be the glory of God, which included your missive as well. After it was read and presented, this reply was sent. God willing, may you ever be blessed with special favors and occupied with that which God has willed. Given the telegram, no further mention was needed or needs to be made.

His honor the beloved Haji Siyyid Javad, upon him be the glory of God, intended to fulfill what you had requested, but permission has not yet been granted since it is Ramadan and the matter of fasting has somewhat delayed social interactions. However, it is hoped that permission will be granted afterwards. In brief, permission has been granted for that beloved one to attain the honor of His presence—whenever you decide, you may proceed. I beseech God, exalted be His glory, that that beloved one may ever be confirmed and assisted.

I convey greetings to the true friends with mention and praise of God, especially to His Holiness Ismu'llah Zayn, upon him be all the most glorious glory, and those with him, and likewise to Aqa Mirza Muhammad and Aqa Mirza Abdullah and Aqa Muhammad Sadiq, upon them be the glory of God, and their brothers, and to Ustad Ali Akbar and Aqa Muhammad Hasan, as well as some of the friends residing in that land who have attained the presence of God. The intention is to convey greetings and salutations to the saints and loved ones of God residing in that land, both men and women.
